mock_response.description:
This entry covers most of the globin family of proteins, but it omits some bacterial globins and the protoglobins.

Globins are haem-containing proteins involved in binding and/or transporting oxygen. They belong to a very large and well studied family that is widely distributed in many organisms [1]. Globins have evolved from a common ancestor and can be divided into three groups: single-domain globins, and two types of chimeric globins, flavohaemoglobins and globin-coupled sensors. Bacteria have all three types of globins, while archaea lack flavohaemoglobins, and eukaryotes lack globin-coupled sensors [2]. Several functionally different haemoglobins can coexist in the same species. The major types of globins include:

description: Look up protein families, domains and sites in InterPro, EMBL-EBI's classification of protein sequences that brings Pfam, CATH-Gene3D and other databases together. Search entries, see which families and domains a UniProt protein or PDB structure contains and where, list the proteins and structures that share one, count them by organism, and browse Pfam clans. No account or API key required.
